title: Exactly four ProviderKind values are driven by ACPSession
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ACPSession.swift:23-25 - doc comment "Drives Agent Client Protocol agents: Cursor, OpenCode, Grok and Devin." on `final class ACPSession: ProviderSession`
DroppyCode/Core/Models/Provider.swift:98 - `var usesACP: Bool { self == .cursor || self == .opencode || self == .grok || self == .devin }`

DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ProviderRegistry.swift:481 - `case .cursor, .opencode, .grok, .devin: try? await ACPSession.probeModels(provider: provider, executable: executable, environment: environment)`
preconditions: A thread is starting a session, or the registry is loading a model catalog.
action: The runtime picks a ProviderSession implementation for the thread's ProviderKind.
expected_result: ACPSession is constructed for exactly .cursor, .opencode, .grok and .devin, and for no other ProviderKind. Display names are "Cursor", "OpenCode", "Grok", "Devin" (Provider.swift:24-30); executable names are "cursor-agent", "opencode", "grok", "devin" (Provider.swift:42-48).
failure_cases: No failure path: the call-site switch is exhaustive over ProviderKind.
windows_path: Same mapping. No platform boundary; provider identity is data.

title: One process-launch gate, shared by every ACP session, spaced 1.5 seconds
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ACPSession.swift:7-21 - `private actor ACPLaunchGate` with `spacing: TimeInterval`, `nextSlot = Date.distantPast`, and `wait()`: `let now = Date.now; let slot = max(now, nextSlot); nextSlot = slot.addingTimeInterval(spacing); if slot > now { try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(slot.timeIntervalSince(now))) }`
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ACPSession.swift:3-6 - rationale: an agent keeps a store of its own (OpenCode's is SQLite); several starting at once trip over its lock, "database is locked"
preconditions: configuration.executable is non-nil, so the guard at :109 has passed.
action: start() awaits the shared launch gate before spawning the child process.
expected_result: Spacing is the literal 1.5 seconds. A lone start never waits, because `slot = max(now, nextSlot)` equals now when nextSlot is in the past. A batch of N starts is released one every 1.5 s. The gate is a single static instance shared across every ACPSession of every provider and every thread, so a Cursor start and an OpenCode start issued together are still spaced 1.5 s apart.
side_effects: Delays process spawn by up to (N-1) * 1.5 s for a batch of N.
persistence: In-memory only: nextSlot lives for the life of the app process.
failure_cases: `try? await Task.sleep` swallows the sleep's error; the wait then returns early and the start proceeds.
cancellation: The sleep's thrown error is discarded by `try?`, so cancelling the awaiting task does not abort the start at this point.
windows_path: A single module-level async mutex holding nextSlot, awaited in the Electron main process before child_process.spawn. It must be one instance for the whole app, not per session, per window or per provider.
verification_method: unit (fake clock: the Nth start releases at (N-1)*1500 ms, a single start at 0 ms)

title: start() refuses before the gate when the provider executable was not resolved
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ProviderSession.swift:158-163 - `.notInstalled` description for non-API-key providers: "\(provider.displayName) is not installed. Install it and sign in with `\(provider.loginCommand)`."
DroppyCode/Core/Models/Provider.swift:62,64,67,68 - loginCommand: cursor "cursor-agent login", opencode "opencode auth login", grok "grok login", devin "devin auth login"
expected_result: start() throws ProviderError.notInstalled(provider) immediately, before the launch gate and before any process is spawned. The user-visible message is exactly "Cursor is not installed. Install it and sign in with `cursor-agent login`." and the OpenCode, Grok and Devin equivalents, with the command wrapped in backticks and a trailing full stop.
windows_path: Same guard. Executable resolution itself is outside PROVACP; PROVACP only sees resolved-or-nil.

title: Child process spawn parameters and framing
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ACPSession.swift:111-116 - `StdioProcess(executable: executable, arguments: launchArguments, directory: configuration.workingDirectory, environment: configuration.environment)`
DroppyCode/Core/Support/StdioProcess.swift:27-40 - init sets executableURL, arguments, currentDirectoryURL, environment and three Pipes; the framing parameter defaults to `.lines`
expected_result: The child is spawned with the resolved executable, the provider and mode argv of PR-PROVACP-005..016, cwd = configuration.workingDirectory, and environment = configuration.environment with no additions, removals or rewrites. Framing is the default `.lines` (newline-delimited JSON), never Content-Length.
side_effects: One external agent CLI process is launched, with stdin, stdout and stderr pipes.
failure_cases: Spawn failure throws out of connection.start() -> process.start(); see PR-PROVACP-018.
windows_path: child_process.spawn(exe, argv, { cwd, env, stdio: ['pipe','pipe','pipe'], shell: false, windowsHide: true }). shell:false is mandatory: tokens such as --permission-mode and --always-approve must not pass through CMD. The env object is passed whole, not merged with process.env, to match `process.environment = environment`.
verification_method: contract fixture (spawn recorder asserting exe, argv array, cwd, env map)

title: Cursor argv, runtime mode .auto
expected_result: argv is exactly the two tokens ["--auto-review", "acp"], in that order.
windows_path: Identical token array passed to spawn with shell:false.

title: Cursor argv, runtime mode .fullAccess
expected_result: argv is exactly ["--force", "acp"].

title: Cursor argv, runtime modes .supervised and .autoAcceptEdits are identical
preconditions: provider == .cursor and configuration.runtimeMode is .supervised or .autoAcceptEdits at launch.
expected_result: argv is exactly the single token ["acp"]. Cursor gets no permission flag for these two modes, so they are indistinguishable on Cursor's command line; the difference is enforced only by ACPSession's own automaticOption (see the automaticOption requirement).

title: Grok argv, runtime mode .supervised
expected_result: argv is exactly the four tokens ["--permission-mode", "default", "agent", "stdio"], in that order, with the flag preceding the `agent` subcommand.

title: Grok argv, runtime mode .autoAcceptEdits uses camelCase acceptEdits
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ACPSession.swift:99 - Devin's equivalent value is the hyphenated "accept-edits"
expected_result: argv is exactly ["--permission-mode", "acceptEdits", "agent", "stdio"]. The value is camelCase acceptEdits with no hyphen. The asymmetry with Devin's accept-edits is a source fact and must be reproduced token for token; normalizing either spelling changes what the CLI is asked for.
failure_cases: A wrong spelling is rejected by the CLI at launch and surfaces as a process exit carrying the CLI's own stderr tail (see the handleClose requirement).
windows_path: Identical token array. Never lowercase or kebab-case the value.
verification_method: unit (argv table test asserting the exact string "acceptEdits")

title: Grok argv, runtime mode .auto
expected_result: argv is exactly ["--permission-mode", "auto", "agent", "stdio"].

title: Grok argv, runtime mode .fullAccess reorders the subcommand and drops --permission-mode
expected_result: argv is exactly the three tokens ["agent", "--always-approve", "stdio"]. Unlike Grok's other three rows the flag sits between the `agent` subcommand and `stdio`, and there is no --permission-mode token at all. Token order is part of the contract.
side_effects: The launched Grok process approves every action on its own side for the life of the process.

title: Devin argv, runtime mode .supervised maps to permission mode auto
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ACPSession.swift:94-96 - comment: Devin's auto approves read-only tools, accept-edits adds workspace edits, smart adds model-judged-safe actions, dangerous approves everything; "Passed before the subcommand, like its CLI expects."
expected_result: argv is exactly ["--permission-mode", "auto", "acp"]. Droppy's .supervised deliberately maps to Devin's `auto`, not to any mode named supervised or default, and the flag precedes `acp`.

title: Devin argv, runtime mode .autoAcceptEdits uses hyphenated accept-edits
expected_result: argv is exactly ["--permission-mode", "accept-edits", "acp"], with the hyphen. Contrast Grok's acceptEdits (PR-PROVACP-009).
verification_method: unit (argv table test asserting the exact string "accept-edits")

title: Devin argv, runtime mode .auto maps to permission mode smart
expected_result: argv is exactly ["--permission-mode", "smart", "acp"].

title: Devin argv, runtime mode .fullAccess maps to permission mode dangerous
expected_result: argv is exactly ["--permission-mode", "dangerous", "acp"]. The literal value is `dangerous`.
side_effects: The launched Devin process approves every action on its own side for the life of the process.

title: OpenCode argv is the bare acp subcommand in every runtime mode
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ACPSession.swift:103-104 - `default: ["acp"]` as the final case of the provider switch
preconditions: provider == .opencode at launch, in any of the four runtime modes.
expected_result: argv is exactly ["acp"] for all four runtime modes. OpenCode receives no permission flag at all; its per-mode behavior comes entirely from automaticOption answering session/request_permission (see the automaticOption requirement).
verification_method: unit (argv table test across all four modes)

title: launchArguments reads the launch-time runtime mode only; a later mode change never relaunches
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ACPSession.swift:78-106 - every branch switches on `configuration.runtimeMode`, the immutable launch configuration, not on the mutable `runtimeMode` property
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ACPSession.swift:38,68 - `private var runtimeMode: RuntimeMode` initialized from configuration.runtimeMode
DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ACPSession.swift:169 - send() assigns `runtimeMode = input.runtimeMode`, updating only the property automaticOption reads
preconditions: A session is running and the user changes the runtime mode.
action: The next turn is sent with a different RuntimeMode.
expected_result: The child process is not restarted and its argv is unchanged. Only self.runtimeMode changes, which alters automaticOption's auto-approval policy from the next permission request onward. The CLI-side permission flag chosen at launch stays in force for the life of the process.
failure_cases: Switching a Grok session from .supervised to .fullAccess does not add --always-approve; only Droppy's own auto-answering changes.
windows_path: Same. Do not add a relaunch-on-mode-change path; per port_impacts #23 the ACP launch flags require a process restart and the source does not perform one.
verification_method: interaction test (change mode mid-session, assert no second spawn)

title: JSON-RPC connection is created with sendsVersion true and three callbacks installed before start
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ACPSession.swift:118-120 - onNotification, onRequest and onClose each assigned with `[weak self]`
DroppyCode/Core/Support/JSONRPC.swift:58-68 - start() calls `try process.start()` then drains process.messages in a Task, calling didClose() when the stream finishes
action: ACPSession wires and starts the connection.
expected_result: Every outbound frame carries "jsonrpc": "2.0". All three callbacks are installed before start, so an inbound request is never answered by the generic -32601 path in JSONRPCConnection; ACPSession's own handler answers it. A spawn failure inside process.start() propagates out of connection.start() and out of start() unchanged.
side_effects: A reader task begins consuming the child's stdout.
failure_cases: Spawn failure: StdioProcess.start() clears both readability handlers, finishes the message stream and rethrows (StdioProcess.swift:74-81); ACPSession.start() propagates it.
windows_path: Same envelope. Per port_impacts #1 and #18, ACP is lines framing WITH the jsonrpc member; do not share an envelope builder with Codex, which omits it.
verification_method: contract fixture (wire recorder asserting every frame carries jsonrpc 2.0)

title: initialize request, verbatim parameters
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/Text.swift:7 - `static let version = Bundle.main.object(forInfoDictionaryKey: "CFBundleShortVersionString") as? String ?? "1.0.0"`
action: ACPSession sends the first request on the connection.
expected_result: Method name is exactly "initialize". protocolVersion is the JSON integer 1, not a string, not 0.1. clientInfo.name is exactly "droppy-code" (lowercase, hyphen), clientInfo.title is exactly "Droppy Code" (space, capitals), clientInfo.version is the app's short version string. The request id is the integer 1 on a fresh connection.
side_effects: One JSON line written to the child's stdin.
failure_cases: An RPC error or a closed process rejects the request and start() throws; the thread reports the RPCError message.
cancellation: Cancelling the awaiting task removes the pending continuation and resumes it with CancellationError (JSONRPC.swift:82-86).
windows_path: Identical payload. The Marrow rename does not change these two literals: name stays "droppy-code" and title stays "Droppy Code", because they are protocol identity fields an agent may key on, not user-visible branding.

title: clientCapabilities declares no filesystem and no terminal capability
expected_result: The object is exactly {"fs": {"readTextFile": false, "writeTextFile": false}, "terminal": false} for a non-Cursor provider. All three values are the JSON boolean false, present rather than omitted. The consequence is that the agent never asks Droppy Code to read or write a file or run a terminal, which is why handleRequest rejects every method except session/request_permission (see the handleRequest requirement).
windows_path: Identical payload. Do not opt into fs or terminal capabilities on Windows to work around anything; the agent CLI does its own file and process work in the cwd.

title: Cursor alone receives the parameterized model picker capability flag
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ACPSession.swift:154-155 - comment: Cursor hides effort and Fast behind this undocumented _meta flag; without it the agent only returns one baked-in variant per model and rejects any other effort
expected_result: For Cursor only, clientCapabilities._meta is {"parameterizedModelPicker": true}. For OpenCode, Grok and Devin the _meta key is absent entirely, not null and not an empty object. The same flag also switches on base-id stripping at :311, :339, :346 and :446.
side_effects: Changes what Cursor reports: model ids come back parameterized as model[effort=high,...], and the effort and Fast config options appear.
failure_cases: Omitting the flag for Cursor silently loses the effort slider and the Fast toggle and makes Cursor reject non-default efforts.
verification_method: contract fixture (two golden initialize frames: Cursor with _meta, OpenCode without)

title: initialize reply: loadSession capability defaults to false
expected_result: canLoadSessions is the boolean at agentCapabilities.loadSession, and false when the key is missing, null or not a boolean. It gates the session/load resume path (PR-PROVACP-028).
failure_cases: A missing capability silently disables resume; no warning is shown.

title: initialize reply: HTTP MCP capability defaults to false and chooses the MCP transport
expected_result: supportsHTTPMCP is agentCapabilities.mcpCapabilities.http, false when absent. False routes HTTP MCP servers through the npx mcp-remote stdio shim instead of a native http entry (PR-PROVACP-026).
windows_path: Same. Downstream consequence to accept: the false branch makes the agent CLI spawn npx as a grandchild that PROVACP neither manages nor kills.

title: initialize reply: authMethods collected as the ids of the advertised methods, in order
expected_result: authMethods is the ordered list of authMethods[].id strings, preserving the agent's order. Entries without a string id are dropped. A missing or non-array authMethods yields an empty list, which disables the auth retry (PR-PROVACP-027).

title: initialize reply may carry a model catalog under _meta.modelState
expected_result: applyModels runs on that value before any session exists, so a .models event can be emitted before session/new. The check is `if let`, so a JSON null value still enters applyModels, where availableModels resolves to an empty list and the `guard !list.isEmpty` at :322 returns without emitting.
side_effects: Possible .models(list, current:) event before the session id exists.
failure_cases: Empty or unparseable model state emits nothing and leaves the previous catalog untouched.
